# Extract: Privacy Policy Key Data Handling Terms

## Data Controller vs. Processor

**Controller:** "The natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of Personal Data"

**Processor:** "The natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which processes personal data on behalf of the Controller"

---

## Message Content Access

The policy states: "Some data may be accessible to certain internal staff (such as administration, sales, marketing, legal, and IT) and to external parties."

For chat interactions: "The data collected in the chatbot will only be used to process your enquiry and will not be passed on to third parties without your express consent."

---

## Encryption

**In Transit:** "We use TLS encryption to secure data transfers on our website"

**At Rest:** No specific encryption-at-rest statement found in the document.

---

## Employee Access

Internal staff with access include: "administration, sales, marketing, legal, and IT"

---

## Sub-processors

"Processors bound by our data protection instructions include service providers. These contractors assist with the processing of data, e.g. for this website. They have been carefully selected and authorised, and are monitored regularly."

An updated list is "available upon request."

---

## Data Retention

General: "We delete or restrict processing of data when it is no longer needed for its intended purpose."

Specific: "Server log files are deleted after 30 days."

CRM data: Reviewed "after two years at the end of each calendar year" for necessity.

# Twilio Data Protection Addendum - Key Extracts

## (1) Data Controller vs. Processor Roles

**Twilio as Controller:**
"Twilio is a processor or sub-processor (acting on behalf of Customer), except where Twilio processes Customer Personal Data as a controller" (Section 2)

**Twilio as Processor:**
"Twilio will process Customer Personal Data as a processor or sub-processor, rather than as a controller" (Section 4.1)

**Customer's Role:**
"Customer may act as a controller or processor on behalf of its End Users" (Section 2)

## (2) Access to Customer Content/Message Content

The document does not explicitly detail who can access message bodies or customer content beyond stating:

"Twilio, as a processor or sub-processor, will process Customer Personal Data in accordance with Customer's instructions" (Schedule 1, Section 5)

Notably, the DPA emphasizes that Twilio processes customer content for abuse detection and legal compliance but doesn't provide granular access controls documentation in this excerpt.

## (3) Encryption at Rest and in Transit

"See Section 12 (Encryption) of the Security Overview" (Schedule 2)

The actual encryption specifications are referenced externally rather than detailed in this addendum itself.

## (4) Employee/Personnel Access Controls

"any person it authorizes to process Customer Personal Data has agreed to protect Customer Personal Data in accordance with Twilio's confidentiality obligations" (Section 5.3)

## (5) Sub-Processors

"Twilio will restrict its sub-processors' access to, and processing of, Customer Personal Data only to what is strictly necessary" (Section 6.1(a))

## (6) Data Retention

**For Standard Services:**
"upon termination of the Agreement, Twilio will...automatically delete any stored Customer Content thirty (30) days after the termination effective date" (Schedule 1, Section 6.1)

**For SendGrid Services:**
"automatically delete any stored Customer Content...one (1) year after the termination effective date" (Schedule 1, Section 6.2)

## Encryption Overview

End-to-end encryption requires all communication to flow through a "device" with a unique phone number, with each side using keys to encrypt and decrypt the payload. WhatsApp messages are encrypted from Twilio to the device, and secured over HTTPS from your application to Twilio, enabling private conversations with your users.

## Cloud API Message Flow

When a user sends a message to a business that uses Cloud API, the message travels encrypted via WhatsApp between the user and Cloud API. Once Cloud API receives the message, Cloud API decrypts the message and forwards it to the business.

For outgoing messages, when a business uses Cloud API to send a message to a user, the reverse applies. Upon receiving a message from a business, Cloud API will encrypt the message using the Signal protocol before sending it to the user via WhatsApp.

## Key Management

In order to send and receive messages through Cloud API, Cloud API manages the encryption/decryption keys on behalf of the business. Per the Signal protocol, the user and Cloud API, acting on behalf of the business, negotiate encryption keys and establish a secure communication channel.

## Webhook Security

Ensure webhook endpoints use HTTPS and validate requests from Twilio using X-Twilio-Signature.

- Security page: "Under no circumstances is sensitive data shared with anyone outside of respond.io and the client." (Note the phrasing — it acknowledges respond.io itself, alongside the client, is inside the access boundary.)

## Bottom line for the two platforms
- **Both are processors, not controllers** (customer/business = controller). Twilio states this explicitly in a public DPA; Respond.io only defines the terms in its Privacy Policy and gates the actual DPA behind an email request — so Respond.io's processor allocation is asserted but NOT publicly verifiable.
- **Both acknowledge platform/employee access to customer data** — neither claims a zero-knowledge / "we can't see your messages" architecture. Twilio: "authorized Twilio employees only." Respond.io: "outside of respond.io and the client" (respond.io is inside the boundary) + named internal staff categories.
- **Both encrypt in transit + at rest** (Twilio: AES at rest / TLS 1.2 in transit; Respond.io: 256-bit AES at rest / 256-bit SSL-TLS in transit).
- **WhatsApp E2E ends at the Cloud API/BSP endpoint** — Meta's own doc confirms Cloud API decrypts the message and forwards it to the business, and manages the keys on the business's behalf. So a WhatsApp BSP like Twilio processes decrypted content; the "end-to-end encryption" marketing does not extend through to the BSP layer.
